title: Hammersmith and Fulham Emergency Help Points
summary: 24/7 emergency hospitals, urgent treatment centres, and local hazards across Hammersmith and Fulham borough.
content:
For immediate life-threatening medical emergencies, always dial 999 first.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals with A&E
- Charing Cross Hospital: Fulham Palace Road, Hammersmith, W6 8RF. From Hammersmith Broadway station: ~12 min walk south along Fulham Palace Road (A219), or take bus 190, 211, 220, or 295.
- Chelsea and Westminster Hospital: 369 Fulham Road, SW10 9NH (serving south Fulham border). From Fulham Broadway station: ~12 min walk east along Fulham Road (A304), or take bus 14 or 414.
- Major Trauma Centre: St Mary's Hospital, Praed Street, Paddington, W2 1NY. From Hammersmith station: Hammersmith & City or Circle line direct to Paddington (~15 mins).

2. Urgent Treatment Centres (Walk-In)
- Charing Cross Urgent Treatment Centre: Fulham Palace Road, Hammersmith, W6 8RF (located inside Charing Cross Hospital A&E entrance). Open 24/7.
- Hammersmith Hospital: Du Cane Road, White City, W12 0HS (specialist acute renal/cardiac services and minor care, not general A&E). From White City station: ~10 min walk north along Wood Lane and Du Cane Road, or bus 72, 272, or 283.

3. Local Area Hazard Notes
- Tidal River Thames: large tidal bend wrapping from Hammersmith Bridge around Sands End and Chelsea Reach. Low riverside spots along Fulham Reach and Bishop's Park face water ingress during high tidal swells and stormwater confluence.

4. Essential Supplies During Outages
Pharmacies and supermarkets situated along King Street (Hammersmith), Fulham Road, North End Road (Fulham), and Shepherd's Bush Green provide bottled water, sanitary goods, and emergency medicines.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
